requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The change deliberately generates a formatter in the consuming assembly for a type from a referenced assembly, which contradicts the earlier convention that referenced-assembly types get no formatter. The new behaviour is explicitly opt-in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] and is what REQ-2129 asks for, so L11 is not violated: TypeCollector's metadata early-return is untouched and no automatic generation occurs.

Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed
Receipts/GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptsTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed

Mutation: 11 killed, 3 survived, 3 compile errors, 0 timeouts (17 mutants on MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs, GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs, ObjectSerializationInfo.cs, GeneratorUtilities.cs, MessagePackGenerator.cs)

findings.claim: The acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. When no SurrogateType is given, Collect always uses CreateContractlessMembers, which ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataContract] and [DataMember] on T. A T marked [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] therefore gets a string-keyed map formatter instead of an int-keyed array formatter, and an [IgnoreMember] property is still serialized. The maintainer's rule was 'if there is no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject] attribute on the type, go contractless', which implies those attributes switch contractless mode off.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests: AttributedReferencedType_IntKeysProduceArrayFormatter and AttributedReferencedType_IgnoreMemberIsNotSerialized fail on head. The generated formatter uses WriteMapHeader and contains 'Secret'.

findings.claim: In the default (no SurrogateType) path, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`. That path ignores every MessagePack attribute on `T`: `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]` and `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` are never read. A `T` with `[IgnoreMember] public string Secret { get; set; }` therefore still has `Secret` serialized. Members marked `[Key(0)]` or `[Key("v")]` are written under their member names as string keys instead of the declared keys. This breaks the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured.' The output is also not byte-compatible with the formatter the defining assembly's own resolver produces.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptsTests.IgnoreMemberOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured. A referenced ProjectA type has [MessagePackObject] with an [IgnoreMember] property `Secret`. The test asserts that the formatter generated for it in ProjectB does not mention `Secret`. On head the contractless path emits `value.Secret`, so the test fails.

findings.claim: `needsCast` compares `m.Name` with "OnBeforeSerialize"/"OnAfterDeserialize" only for methods that have ExplicitInterfaceImplementations. An explicit implementation's Name is the qualified "MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize", so the check never matches. It also inspects only `type.GetMembers()`, not base types, and private explicit impls are not imported from metadata. As a result, any `T` that implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver explicitly gets `needsCast = false`. The template then emits `value.OnBeforeSerialize()`, which fails to compile (CS1061) in the generated code.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptsTests.ExplicitCallbackReceiverCompiles. It runs the generator over a type that explicitly implements IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver and has a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter for it. It then asserts the updated compilation has no errors. On head this fails with CS1061 in the generated formatter.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode silently drops public get-only properties and does not honour [IgnoreDataMember] on T. That differs from MessagePack's existing contractless behaviour over public members, which writes get-only public properties. The same object would serialize to different bytes through the generated formatter than through ContractlessStandardResolver.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize an instance of a referenced class that has a public get-only property and a read-write property in two ways: with ContractlessStandardResolver, and with the head-generated [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter. Compare the bytes; the map entry count and keys differ.

hunches.claim: The generated partial class is emitted with only the 'partial class' modifiers. It is emitted inside EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and carries the generic constraints and formatter name from Info.Formatter. The analyzer never checks whether the user's declaration is a class nested in a generic or static container, or is 'sealed' or 'static'. The accessibility of the formatter, which is user-declared, does not matter for the partial. The main compatibility risk is the resolver: the generated resolver registers Info.Formatter as if it were a generated 'internal sealed' class. A user-declared public formatter may be instantiated through a different path, such as 'new Formatter()'. The user-declared formatter may also lack a parameterless constructor, which would break the generated resolver.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class that has a custom constructor, then compile the generated resolver and check that it still builds.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode serializes members sorted by ordinal name and silently drops get-only or private-set properties, readonly fields and init-only properties that would normally be serialized. Because IsPublicReadWrite requires a public setter, init-only properties are included (their SetMethod is public) while the info is marked IsInitOnly. The sort order is name-ordinal, whereas the existing contractless resolver uses declaration order. Bytes for a type serialized through this formatter therefore differ from the dynamic ContractlessStandardResolver for the same type, which breaks interoperability for users who later switch resolvers. This follows from the requirement but is not documented.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with properties {Zed, Alpha, Mid} through a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class, then through ContractlessStandardResolver. Compare the map key order bytes.

hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities hand-written-formatter filter matches the attribute by display string. If the attribute is absent, no problem arises. If the user's formatter has the attribute but the generator rejects it (not partial, wrong interface), the formatter is dropped from the hand-written registration too. A previously working hand-written formatter that gains the attribute would silently lose resolver registration.

receipt_plan.detail: Snapshot test: a non-partial class with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T>. Check that the generated resolver neither registers it nor produces a compile error beyond MsgPack019.

hunches.claim: Deleting the `!symbol.GetAttributes().Any(... GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute)` guard would register the generated formatter twice (as a hand-written formatter and as an ObjectSerializationInfo). No test fails, because the execution tests only check GetFormatter<T>() and round trips, and the generator snapshot tests don't cover this path.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: `&& !symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` -> removed; expected to survive because tests only assert GetFormatter<T>() type and round-trip behavior, and GeneratedMessagePackResolver would still compile or return the formatter, so no duplicate-registration assertion exists

hunches.claim: The dedicated generator tests only cover diagnostics. No snapshot or regeneration test verifies the emitted code for the integer-key template or the string-key template (`partial class` vs `internal sealed class`). Swapping the IsUserDeclaredFormatter ternary in either template or the Info.IsUserDeclaredFormatter flag in Collect would only be caught indirectly by the execution tests. Struct and int-key coverage are also thin.

"partial class" : "internal sealed class" -> inverted; the execution-test project would fail to compile, but the SourceGenerator.Tests snapshots for generated output would not notice because none exist for this attribute

hunches.claim: The collector diagnostics have no tests: inaccessible data type, generic data type, class without a parameterless constructor (MsgPack006), a surrogate member missing [Key] (MsgPack004), duplicate keys (MsgPack006/KeysMustBeUnique), and a read-only or private target member. Removing any of those guards in GeneratedFormatterCollector survives.

hunches.claim: The contractless tests don't cover private-member exclusion, public fields, read-only fields, or inherited members, and no test checks that existing MessagePack attributes on T are honoured, which the acceptance criteria require. The ExternalPerson type has only one read-only property, and no test hits the ordering, IsPublicReadWrite field branch, or the base-type walk in GetInstanceMembers.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:226 swap-boolean: `!field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst` -> `field.IsReadOnly || field.IsConst`; expected to survive because no external test type has a public field

hunches.claim: Surrogate and contractless tests exercise only int keys with no gaps, or string keys. There is no test for the string-key surrogate path, the `members.Count` fallback index, or MsgPack005 (mixed keys) in a compiled run. The mixed-key test asserts MsgPack005 only, and a mutation of the key-kind check would not be exercised in the passing-surrogate tests.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:157 off-by-one: `intKey: members.Count` -> `members.Count + 1`; expected to survive because no execution test uses a string-key surrogate

hunches.claim: Diagnostics are reported through a separate generator pipeline that has no test for the happy path (no spurious diagnostics). Also, with ReferenceSymbols.TryCreate failing, no diagnostic is reported silently. The MsgPack019 test uses a nonpartial class, which has its own compile errors masked by the hand-written Members.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:127 delete-statement: context.RegisterSourceOutput(generatedFormatterDiagnostics, ...) deleted; expected to be killed by MsgPack019/020/021/022 tests, so the real gap is the absent negative test that valid formatters produce no diagnostics

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration. Containing types are not checked. A formatter nested in a non-partial class (`class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> { } }`) passes validation, and the template then emits `partial class F` inside the nesting from EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces. If that nesting reproduces Outer, the output fails with CS0260 (missing partial on Outer) instead of an MsgPack019/MsgPack011-style diagnostic. A private nested formatter is also accepted even though the generated resolver must instantiate it.

receipt_plan.detail: IsPartial (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs, end of file) inspects only the ClassDeclarationSyntax of `formatter`. No check walks formatter.ContainingType for the partial modifier or for accessibility from the resolver. Confirm by generating for a formatter nested in a non-partial class and compiling the output.

hunches.claim: Each [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] model is added to `modelPerType` unconditionally. If `T` is also a [MessagePackObject] type in the same compilation, or two generated formatters target the same `T`, two ObjectSerializationInfos for the same data type reach the resolver. Depending on the resolver template and the ObjectInfos comparer, this either drops one formatter silently (sorted-set dedupe) or registers `typeof(T)` twice in the resolver lookup, which throws at type initialization. No diagnostic is reported for the duplicate.

receipt_plan.detail: MessagePackGenerator.cs:70-76 adds the generated model without checking for an existing ObjectInfo with the same DataType. Generate for a source type that has [MessagePackObject] together with a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class for that same type, then inspect the generated resolver.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change implements the formatter-class attribute with contractless default plus an optional SurrogateType property (the maintainer's suggested design). Keys come from the surrogate's [Key] and [IgnoreMember] attributes, matched by member name. Only parameterless constructors and public read-write members are supported.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Support only the minimal contractless mode, with no SurrogateType. Honour attributes already on T (DataContract, DataMember, MessagePackObject, Key) and use no surrogate. This requires removing the SurrogateType property, the surrogate collector path and MsgPack022, and adding handling for attributes present on T.
